# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 👎 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🫴]
Blind gestures: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

**Thinking.**

I am Deaf. I see everything printed on the bomb and nothing reaches me by ear, so both teammates can hear me but only Mute can reach me, by gesture. The bomb in front of me: display reads 0, the light is green, and there are three wires — one yellow, two green, three red.

What just arrived: Mute signed to me directly — hello, yes, no, one, two, three, then a palm-up "hand it over" — which reads as a proposed vocabulary plus a request for the bomb's state. Blind signed hello and one-two-three, almost certainly the same counting idea, or announcing the three wires Blind can feel. I adopt that code: 👍 yes/correct, 👎 no/wrong, ☝ one, ✌ two, 🤟 three, 👋 greeting.

The crucial structural fact: Mute holds the manual but cannot speak, and Blind holds the hands but cannot see gestures. Mute and Blind cannot reach each other at all. I am the only bridge — Mute must gesture instructions to me, and I must speak them aloud to Blind. So my first job is a complete spoken report of everything visible, addressed to both, plus a signed confirmation to Mute that the code is agreed and the request was received. Colors and numbers travel by voice only, since gestures cannot carry them.

```
speak(text="Hello, this is Deaf. I can see the bomb and I cannot hear, so reach me only with gestures. Full report of what I see: the display reads zero. The light is green. There are three wires in order: wire one is yellow, wire two is green, wire three is red. Mute: I received your signs and I accept your code — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, one, two, three. Mute, remember Blind cannot see your gestures, so every instruction you have must come through me and I will speak it to Blind. Blind: I am your voice for Mute. Nobody act until Mute has matched the manual to this report.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "👍", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 ☝ ✌ 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Thinking.**

Two acknowledgments came in. Mute signed back hello–yes–one-two-three: the code is mutually agreed. Blind sent a thumbs up: Blind heard my spoken report and confirmed receipt — and crucially, Mute heard it too, because Mute cannot speak but Mute *can* hear. My spoken report last round reached both teammates. So everyone now holds the bomb state: display 0, light green, wires yellow/green/red.

The remaining gaps: Blind doesn't know which physical wire is "one" — Blind must map my numbering onto touch. And Mute has the manual plus the full state, so Mute should now be ready to speak the actual instruction aloud to Blind next round (speech is Mute's only channel to Blind; Blind cannot see signs). I also need a way for Mute to query me for visual details, since Mute's questions can only reach me as gestures: I propose item-number plus the pinched-fingers sign as "tell me everything about this." And until a manual step is spoken, nobody touches anything — a wrong move is fatal.

I confirm to Mute by sign (Mute sees it), and say the rest aloud for both. When I write 🤌 into my sentence, Mute will see the exact sign; Blind will only hear my verbal description of it, which is fine — it's not for Blind.

```
speak(text="Both replies received. Mute, I see your signs: agreed, our number code is one, two, three. Blind, I saw your thumbs up — you cannot see any of these signs, so anything that concerns you I will always say out loud. Blind, here is the wire orientation: the wire I called one is the leftmost, two is the middle, three is the rightmost, on the bomb as it faces you. Please confirm by touch that you feel exactly three wires, and whether anything on it turns, clicks, or slides before we commit to any action. Mute, you heard my full report: display zero, light green, wire one yellow, wire two green, wire three red. You hold the manual. When you have found the matching rule, speak it directly to Blind next round — do not gesture it, Blind cannot see signs. If you need any more detail from the bomb — any label, marking, port, or the exact appearance of the display — gesture the item's number and then the pinched-fingers sign, 🤌, addressed to me, and I will answer aloud with everything visible. Until Mute speaks the instruction, nobody cuts, presses, or moves anything. Current status unchanged: display still zero, light still green.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]

**Thinking.**

Parsing arrivals. Mute signed hello–yes–three; Blind signed yes–no. Blind is answering my two touch questions in order: yes, three wires are felt; no, nothing turns, clicks, or slides. I'll state that reading aloud and ask for correction.

Now the hard structural truth I got wrong last round: I told Mute to *speak* the instruction to Blind — but Mute cannot speak, ever. Mute's only output is gesture, and Blind cannot see gesture. So nothing Mute knows can reach Blind except through me: Mute spells to me in signs, I voice it to Blind. And since I'm deaf, Blind's speech never reaches *me* — so Blind must keep answering me in signs, and use spoken words only toward Mute (who hears). The channels: Mute→me by sign, me→Blind by voice, Blind→Mute by voice, Blind→me by sign.

Ambiguous tokens like Mute's lone "three" are too dangerous for a no-retry bomb. Mute hears everything I say, so I can teach a full spelling code aloud: 26 letter-signs, plus space and end-of-message signs, on top of our agreed status signs. Then Mute can spell any manual rule verbatim, I relay it word for word, Blind repeats it aloud for Mute to confirm with thumbs up before touching anything. The board is static (display still 0, light still green), so there is time to build this properly — and I explicitly hold Blind's hands until a confirmed instruction arrives.

```
speak(text="Status unchanged: display zero, light green, wire one yellow, wire two green, wire three red. Blind: I read your two signs as — yes, you feel exactly three wires; no, nothing turns, clicks, or slides. If that is wrong, correct me next round with signs to me: thumbs up or down, numbers. Keep answering me in signs, because I am deaf and never hear your voice — but do speak out loud toward Mute when you repeat instructions back, because Mute can hear you. Mute: I made an error earlier when I asked you to speak — you cannot speak, forget that. New plan, and since you can hear me, learn this code. Our standing signs remain: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, one, two, three as numbers, pinched fingers means question or tell me details, closed fist means stop or hold, OK sign means ready. Now the letter code, one sign per letter, so you can spell any word from the manual to me: A is 🤚, B is 🖖, C is 🤏, D is 🫳, E is 🫴, F is 🫱, G is 🫲, H is 🫷, I is 🫸, J is 🤛, K is 🤜, L is 👊, M is 🖐, N is ✋, O is 🫰, P is 🤘, Q is 🤙, R is 👏, S is 🙌, T is 🫶, U is 👐, V is 🤲, W is 🤝, X is 🙏, Y is 🫵, Z is ✍. The raised hand with splayed little finger and thumb, 🤳, means a space between words, and the nail-polish sign, 💅, means end of message. Mute: next round, spell out first what your lone three meant, then the manual rule that matches this bomb — display zero, light green, wires yellow, green, red. Spell it letter by letter and I will voice it to Blind exactly as you wrote it. Blind: touch nothing until you hear me relay Mute's complete spelled instruction. When you do hear it, repeat it aloud word for word so Mute hears it and can confirm with thumbs up to me; only after that confirmation do you act.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "👍", "👌"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤏 👐 🫶 🤳 🤝 🫸 👏 🫴 🤳 🫶 🫷 👏 🫴 🫴 🤳 🤟 👍 💅]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👌]

**Thinking.**

Decoding Mute's message against the letter code I taught last round: 🤏 👐 🫶 = C-U-T, 🤳 space, 🤝 🫸 👏 🫴 = W-I-R-E, 🤳 space, 🫶 🫷 👏 🫴 🫴 = T-H-R-E-E, then 🤟 three, 👍 yes, 💅 end. The greeting 👋 and the spaces and terminator landed exactly where my code put them, so Mute has fully adopted the system. The message reads: **"CUT WIRE THREE — yes."** This also explains Mute's lone 🤟 from last round: it was the start of this answer. The instruction is consistent with everything so far, and Mute has the manual plus my full report (display 0, green light, wires yellow/green/red), so this is the manual's verdict: cut the third wire, which is the red one, rightmost.

Blind signed 👍 👌 — yes, ready — but Blind has not yet heard the instruction; that was just confirmation of my last spoken turn and general readiness. So the relay now happens this round.

Protocol before anyone touches anything: I voice the instruction verbatim to Blind. Blind repeats it aloud (Mute hears — that's the only error-check possible, since Mute cannot see signs and Blind cannot see them either). Mute confirms or rejects by gesture to me; I voice the final "cut" command. One extra round on a bomb with no second attempt is cheap, and the board is static — display still 0, light still green, four turns running.

I also flag the wire identification carefully: Blind must count from the left edge of the bomb — third wire, nearest the right edge — because Blind cannot verify the colour red. And I ask Mute whether any further step or condition exists, since "cut wire three" alone might not be the whole rule.

```
speak(text="Mute's instruction is decoded and here it is, word for word: cut wire three. Blind, that means you: identify the wires by counting from the left edge of the bomb as it faces you — the leftmost wire is one, the middle is two, the third and rightmost is three. Wire three is the red one. Tool-cut wire three only. Nothing else — do not touch the display, the light, or the other two wires. Blind, before you act: repeat this instruction aloud now, word for word, so Mute can hear your repeat-back and verify it. Then wait — do not cut yet. Mute: I have relayed your instruction to Blind exactly as you spelled it. When you hear Blind repeat it back, gesture thumbs up to me if it is correct, thumbs down to me if anything is wrong, and I will voice the final go-ahead to Blind. Also, Mute: if the manual requires any further step, condition, or action after the cut, spell it to me the same way. If cutting wire three is the entire instruction, gesture the OK sign to me and nothing more. Status check: display zero, light green, all three wires intact.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✌", "👌"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Thinking.**

Mute sent 👍 👌: the repeat-back was verified correct, and cutting wire three is the entire instruction — nothing before it, nothing after it. Blind sent 👍: ready and holding. The full chain is now verified: Mute's manual verdict matched against my visual report, relayed verbatim to Blind, repeated back aloud, and confirmed by the only one who has read the rule. Every channel has been checked at both ends. Time to give the go-ahead.

The command must be exact and unambiguous, since Blind acts on voice alone: cut the third wire counting from the left, the rightmost, the red one. Cut only that. Then report back to me in signs, because I cannot hear the outcome spoken.

```
speak(text="Blind — the instruction has been verified by Mute against the manual. You are cleared to act. Final command: cut wire three. That is the third wire counting from the left edge, the rightmost wire, the red one. Use the cutter and cut that one wire only. Do not touch wire one or wire two, the display, or the light. Cut it now. When it is done, answer me in signs: thumbs up to me if the bomb appears neutralized — display frozen, light off, no sound of any mechanism — thumbs down if anything changes for the worse. I will relay the outcome to Mute. That is all: one cut, wire three, rightmost, red.")
```
